output.summary: The rise in admitted-patient ED length of stay is almost entirely boarding (about 3.0 of 3.2 hours, E5). ED work-up time barely moved. Nurse staffing is stable by independent payroll data: hours per visit are flat, vacancy fell, and 97% of shifts meet the grid (E4). Volume, acuity and admission rate are flat (E3). That contradicts the CNO's understaffing claim. The jump coincides with the March hospitalist rounding change, which plausibly delays discharges on the medical wards (E6). Discharge-time data is missing, so the rounding link is not established. Bed capacity and the September cleaning cut are untested. Extending the early-discharge huddle is cheap and reversible. The travel-nurse contract and pausing the huddle would work against the likely mechanism.
